title: Construct Quad-Tree
statement_short: Given a n x n matrix of 0's and 1's, construct a Quad-Tree representing the matrix. If a grid block contains uniform values, create a leaf node; otherwise, divide the grid into four equal quadrant sub-blocks recursively.
constraints: n == grid.length == grid[i].length, n == 2^x where 0 <= x <= 6, grid[i][j] is 0 or 1
hint: Grid dimension n = 2^x (n <= 64) permits 4-way recursive divide-and-conquer region checks.
keywords: divide the grid into four equal quadrant sub-blocks
why_not: Right: Tree DFS recursively checks region uniformity and constructs four quad-children in O(n^2 log n) time. Not 2D DP: Dynamic programming caches subproblems, but grid region partitioning requires top-down tree construction. Not Tree BFS: Level-order traversal builds tree levels, but top-down recursive quad-splitting naturally uses DFS. Not Union-Find: Disjoint sets merge connected cells, but Quad-Trees represent hierarchical spatial grid partitioning.
complexity: O(n^2 log n) time, O(log n) space
